note: Movements that tend to load, or be limited by, each kind of injury. General guidance for planning, not clinical clearance. First matching rule wins. {S}/{s} is the injured side (Right/right) and {O}/{o} the opposite side. Edit freely.

rules.name: Patellar tendon / patella
rules.basis: Van der Worp et al. 2014 (systematic review): horizontal landing after forward acceleration carries the greatest risk; stiff landing patterns linked to onset.

rules.name: Achilles / calf / soleus
moves: Explosive toe-off when driving or cutting
sided: Push-off from the {s} leg when driving or cutting
rules.basis: General reasoning; Habets et al. 2017 (review) describes running and jumping as the activities held back until Achilles symptoms settle.

rules.name: Hamstring
moves: Hard deceleration with a straight leg
Long strides and lunging forward (stretch under load)
rules.basis: Late-swing review (Scand J Med Sci Sports 2019): the most likely injury phase in high-speed running is late swing.

rules.name: Groin / adductor
moves: Quick cuts and crossovers in a wide stance
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.

rules.name: Quadriceps / hip flexor
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.

rules.name: Hip / glute
moves: Deep defensive stance and lateral slides
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.

rules.name: Ankle
moves: Cutting and change of direction (sideways loads)
Landing from jumps, especially contested or uneven landings
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.

rules.name: Foot / toe

sided: Push-off from the {s} foot when driving or cutting
